---
title: "onthesignal"
subtitle: "Signal processing for the characterization of seismic acquisition chains"
---

onthesignal measures what a seismic acquisition chain really does: digitizer self-noise and
dynamic range, sine-wave performance (SINAD, ENOB, SFDR, THD, SNR), comparison with the
Peterson noise models, time measurements, coherence and spectrograms. It runs as an
interactive console in a Linux terminal and reads miniSEED and text files, or acquires data
from SeedLink servers.

This documentation has three parts:

| Part | For | Content |
|---|---|---|
| [User manual](user/index.qmd) | everyone | installation, console, commands, measurement procedures, reports, AI assistant |
| [Algorithms](algorithms/index.qmd) | metrologists, reviewers | definitions, equations, implementation, limits and validation of every computation |
| [Developer guide](developer/index.qmd) | contributors | architecture, adding an analysis, conventions, tests |

The [API reference](reference/index.qmd) is generated from the docstrings, and the
[AI functions](ai/agent.md) page is the file given to the AI assistant.

## Building this documentation

```bash
cd docs
QUARTO_PYTHON=../.venv/bin/python ../.venv/bin/quartodoc build
QUARTO_PYTHON=../.venv/bin/python quarto render
```

The pages of the *Algorithms* part contain Python cells executed at render time: their
figures are always produced by the current code.
